text:
lee: Hey all, just joined today! Trying to get dev env parity between my M2 Mac and a WSL Ubuntu VM. Followed the quickstart but running into build failures when installing Ruby and some native npm modules. Error snippets below, any quick tips?

> ld: library not found for -lssl
> make: *** [ext.so] Error 1
> npm ERR! code 1

harper: welcome! common culprits: openssl path on Apple Silicon and missing pkg-config/build deps on WSL. Quick flow that worked for me:
1) brew install asdf openssl@3 pkg-config automake autoconf libtool
2) set env before building Ruby/gems:
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib/pkgconfig"
export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"
# then `asdf install ruby 3.2.2` or whatever pinned version

On WSL: `sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y build-essential libssl-dev zlib1g-dev pkg-config libffi-dev` before asdf/ruby install.

harper: For npm native modules that call Rust (image libs, certain crypto packages), install rustup and set ~/.cargo/bin on PATH. Also install `python3` (some node-gyp builds require it).

lee: I also saw a complaint about pkg-config missing when building node-sass type packages. Installing pkg-config fixed it on WSL.

harper: Right. One extra gotcha: on mac, some people have multiple OpenSSLs (brew, macports). Make sure the flags point to the brew one. Running `pkg-config --cflags openssl` should show the include path.

lee: Where should I stash REDWOOD_API_KEY and KUBECONFIG so scripts pick them up but I don't accidentally commit them?

harper: Don't commit secrets. We use direnv + a local config file by convention. Example pattern: create `~/.config/redwood/env.local` (gitignored) with:
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-local-xxxx
export REDWOOD_ENV=dev
export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config-redwood
Then in repo `.envrc` add `source_env ~/.config/redwood/env.local`. direnv keeps it out of git and auto-loads.

lee: How do I get the kubeconfig for the dev cluster?

infra: Please fill the onboarding access form (pinned in #new-hires) and request "dev-cluster kubeconfig." Ops will provision a per-user kube context and send a secure link. When you get it, either set `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config-redwood` or merge it via `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/.kube/config-redwood kubectl config view --raw > ~/.kube/config-merged` then `mv` into place.

ops-bot: Created ticket INF-5027 for lee to receive kube and repo access.

lee: SSH key question: I have ed25519 and an rsa for legacy; which do you prefer?

harper: ed25519 is preferred. Add the public key to your GitHub account. For internal deploy keys, infra will guide you if a repo needs a specific key; otherwise GitHub org access is sufficient.

lee: one last thing 1: any recommended dotfiles bits?

harper: Clone our starter: `github.com/redwood-onboarding/dotfiles-starter`. It has asdf init lines, direnv examples, and a sample `~/.gitconfig`. Add to your shell rc:
. $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh
eval "$(direnv hook zsh)"
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"

lee: great, i'll try the openssl flags + rustup and post logs if i'm still blocked. thanks! :rocket:
